target.title: policy: cover gateway node commands
target.body:
## Summary - add policy evidence for `gateway.nodes.allowCommands` and `gateway.nodes.denyCommands` entries - add `gateway.nodes.denyCommands` policy metadata and shape validation - report `policy/gateway-node-command-denied` when policy-denied node commands are not denied by OpenClaw config - document the new policy rule in the Policy CLI and plugin reference docs - classify `gateway.nodes.allowCommands.*` in policy config coverage  ## Policy syntax / evidence / finding contract  Policy syntax added by this PR:  ```jsonc {   "gateway": {     "nodes": {       "denyCommands": ["system.run"]     }   } } ```  `gateway.nodes.denyCommands` is an exact, case-sensitive deny-superset rule. An equal-or-stricter policy must include every command required by the baseline deny list. Empty or missing `denyCommands` means this rule is not active.  OpenClaw config evidence collected by policy doctor:  ```jsonc {   "gateway": {     "nodes": {       "allowCommands": ["mcp.help", "mcp.invoke", "system.run"],       "denyCommands": ["system.run"]     }   } } ```  The evidence scanner records concrete config entries as:  ```text kind=nodeAllowCommand command=system.run source=oc://openclaw.config/gateway/nodes/allowCommands/#2 kind=nodeDenyCommand  command=system.run source=oc://openclaw.config/gateway/nodes/denyCommands/#0 ```  Finding emitted when policy requires a deny but config does not provide it:  ```json {   "checkId": "policy/gateway-node-command-denied",   "severity": "error",   "message": "Gateway node command 'system.run' is denied by policy but not denied by OpenClaw config.",   "path": "openclaw config",   "ocPath": "oc://openclaw.config/gateway/nodes/denyCommands",   "target": "oc://openclaw.config/gateway/nodes/denyCommands",   "requirement": "oc://policy.jsonc/gateway/nodes/denyCommands",   "fixHint": "Add 'system.run' to gateway.nodes.denyCommands or update policy after review." } ```  The finding clears when the config deny list contains the required exact command id. `allowCommands` evidence is collected for coverage and context; this PR only enforces the policy deny-superset contract.  ## Real behavior proof  Behavior or issue addressed: Managed policy can now require privileged gateway node commands such as `system.run` to be denied in OpenClaw config via `gateway.nodes.denyCommands`. The policy doctor reports the missing config deny and clears once the config denylist covers the policy denylist.  Real environment tested: Windows 11 PowerShell, `C:\src\openclaw-fork` checkout at PR head `cfe901e17963d9fe1833266a2758f125d7a51762`, source-harness invocation of the real policy doctor health checks through `runDoctorLintChecks`. The harness wrote real temporary `openclaw.jsonc` and `policy.jsonc` files under `%TEMP%`; no cloud gateway or Lobster deployment was involved.  Exact steps or command run after this patch: 1. Ran a Node/tsx source harness from the repo root that imported `registerPolicyDoctorChecks` and `runDoctorLintChecks`. 2. Case `missing-config-deny`: wrote `policy.jsonc` with `gateway.nodes.denyCommands: ["system.run"]` and `openclaw.jsonc` with `gateway.nodes.allowCommands: ["mcp.help", "mcp.invoke", "system.run"]` and no config `denyCommands`. 3. Case `satisfied-config-deny`: wrote the same policy plus `openclaw.jsonc` with `gateway.nodes.denyCommands: ["system.run"]`.  Evidence after fix: ```text CASE missing-config-deny workspace: C:\Users\giodl\AppData\Local\Temp\oc-policy-missing-config-deny-Xk9xXX openclaw.jsonc gateway.nodes: {"allowCommands":["mcp.help","mcp.invoke","system.run"]} policy.jsonc gateway.nodes.denyCommands: ["system.run"] finding.checkId: policy/gateway-node-command-denied finding.severity: error finding.message: Gateway node command 'system.run' is denied by policy but not denied by OpenClaw config. finding.ocPath: oc://openclaw.config/gateway/nodes/denyCommands finding.target: oc://openclaw.config/gateway/nodes/denyCommands finding.requirement: oc://policy.jsonc/gateway/nodes/denyCommands finding.fixHint: Add 'system.run' to gateway.nodes.denyCommands or update policy after review.  CASE satisfied-config-deny workspace: C:\Users\giodl\AppData\Local\Temp\oc-policy-satisfied-config-deny-jngRgn openclaw.jsonc gateway.nodes: {"allowCommands":["mcp.help","mcp.invoke","system.run"],"denyCommands":["system.run"]} policy.jsonc gateway.nodes.denyCommands: ["system.run"] policy/gateway-node-command-denied findings: none ```  Observed result after fix: The missing config-deny case emits exactly one `policy/gateway-node-command-denied` error targeted at `oc://openclaw.config/gateway/nodes/denyCommands`. The satisfied config-deny case emits no finding for that check.  What was not tested: This was source-harness policy doctor proof, not a live Lobster/cloud gateway run. Cloud gateway rollout behavior for `system.run` allowlisting remains a separate Lobster deployment concern.  ## Validation - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/policy/src/doctor/register.test.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/strictness.test.ts --reporter=dot` - `node --import tsx scripts/check-policy-config-coverage.ts --check --json` - `./node_modules/oxfmt/bin/oxfmt --check extensions/policy/src/doctor/metadata.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/scopes/gateway.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/register.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/register.test.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/strictness.test.ts extensions/policy/src/policy-state.ts scripts/lib/policy-config-coverage.jsonc` - `./node_modules/oxlint/bin/oxlint extensions/policy/src/doctor/metadata.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/scopes/gateway.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/register.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/register.test.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/strictness.test.ts extensions/policy/src/policy-state.ts` - `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt.cmd --check docs/cli/policy.md docs/plugins/reference/policy.md extensions/policy/src/doctor/metadata.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/scopes/gateway.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/register.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/register.test.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/strictness.test.ts extensions/policy/src/policy-state.ts scripts/lib/policy-config-coverage.jsonc` - `node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs docs README.md` - `git diff --check` - `pnpm tsgo:test:extensions` - `codex review --base upstream/main`  ## Notes This gives managed policy a way to require privileged gateway node commands such as `system.run` to be present in `gateway.nodes.denyCommands` unless a deployment intentionally relaxes policy. The rule uses the existing `denylist-superset` strictness pattern and keeps node command IDs case-sensitive.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed:
Gateway node command policy coverage stays intact after restacking onto current `upstream/main`; the stack also resolves the `plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts` merge conflict by preserving CI budget-env isolation.

Real environment tested:
Windows PowerShell in `C:\src\openclaw-fork` on the restacked policy series, top head `283c1bb4ca` with the foundation branch head `86e2ee92f4`. This is a source-harness proof; it does not start a packaged OpenClaw binary or make live LLM calls.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
1. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/policy/src/doctor/metadata.test.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/register.test.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/strictness.test.ts src/flows/doctor-repair-flow.test.ts --reporter=dot`
2. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts --reporter=dot`
3. `pnpm tsgo:extensions`
4. `pnpm lint:extensions`
5. `git diff --check`

Evidence after fix:
The focused policy/core Vitest run passed 10 core repair-flow tests and 297 policy doctor tests. The SDK surface tooling test passed 7 tests. `tsgo:extensions`, `lint:extensions`, and `git diff --check` all exited 0.

Observed result after fix:
Gateway node command policy coverage remains green, and the restacked branch no longer has the generated SDK surface test conflict against current `main`.

What was not tested:
No packaged CLI smoke, live provider run, or live LLM call was run for this restack proof.
